grade.rationale: The navigation update is concise and dependency-injected, but the embedded-message boundary has two material security and correctness weaknesses: it discloses the complete current URL and explicitly permits delivery regardless of the parent origin.

summary: The function correctly updates preview parameters and is straightforward to test through its environment abstraction. However, its postMessage contract contradicts the stated data-minimization boundary by forwarding arbitrary existing URL content, and the wildcard target origin prevents authenticating the recipient. ESLint evidence was unavailable, and test coverage remains unknown.

grade.rationale: URL parameter updates work, but embedded reporting may disclose unrelated query parameters, fragments, or credentials to an unauthenticated parent origin.
The implementation is compact and uses explicit interfaces and constants, though the target-origin contract hard-codes an unsafe policy that callers cannot improve.
Names and control flow are clear, but the documentation's claim that the message carries no credentials is not enforced by the implementation.

URL construction and environment operations can throw without contextual handling, although propagation may be appropriate for these synchronous adapter operations; the more significant issue is failure to constrain the messaging boundary.
Injecting href, history replacement, and parent messaging makes behavior readily unit-testable. Coverage is unknown rather than absent.

findings.title: Parent messages are sent without validating the recipient origin
findings.description: The message is always sent with `'*'` as its target origin, and the environment interface only permits that literal value. Any origin capable of embedding the preview can therefore receive its navigation messages, while a parent navigation race could also redirect a message to a different origin. This is especially risky because the payload contains a complete URL.
findings.recommendation: Determine an expected parent origin from trusted configuration or a validated embedding handshake, expose it through the environment contract, and pass that exact origin to `postMessage`. Reject or disable embedded reporting when no trusted origin is available.

findings.title: Navigation message exposes arbitrary existing URL data
findings.description: `url.href` includes the origin, fragment, user-information if present, and every pre-existing query parameter—not just `path`, `kind`, and `repo`. Consequently, the implementation cannot uphold the documented promise that the message carries no credentials or other sensitive content; tokens or unrelated state already present in `environment.href` would be forwarded to the parent.
findings.recommendation: Construct the reported URL from an allowlist of required navigation fields and an explicitly approved origin/path. Exclude unrelated query parameters, user-information, and the fragment unless each is part of the documented protocol.
